newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal opposition to let budget pass. [CORRECTED 13:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Portugal opposition to let budget pass. [CORRECTED 13:51 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects attribution in headline and throughout story to make clear prime minister made comments, not Popular Party leader).

Portugal's small opposition Popular Party (PP) reached an agreement on Wednesday with the minority ruling Socialists that would ensure the government's budget passed its final parliamentary test, Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said. "The accord...is that the PP is going to ensure that the budget passes in the final vote," Prime Minister Antonio Guterres told journalists.

Guterres, who spoke to reporters after meeting Popular Party leader Manuel Monteiro, said that the Popular Party would not necessarily cast its ballot in favour of the budget when it is voted on next week, as abstaining would be enough.
The Popular Party has 15 representatives in the 230-seat chamber where the government is four seats short of an outright majority.

The 1997 deficit-cutting budget package is vital to Portugal's chances of qualifying for the European Union's planned single currency and its eventual approval by parliament has never really been in doubt.
The largest opposition party, the Social Democrats, who share the Socialists' commitment to Europe, abstained when parliament voted on the general outlines of the plan last month.
Parliament will vote on December 12 on the individual measures contained in the budget package.
